definition: An odorous quality inhering in a plant structure by virtue of its having an odour of garlic or onion.
reason: A distinct, diagnostic odour (e.g. Scorodophloeus, Afrostyrax bark and seed); sibling of the FLOPO odour values sweet-scented, spicy-scented and foetid, and no PATO term exists.
A compound of two surface values, and neither part has a fitting term: PATO granular is a composition quality (containing granules), not a surface texture. Too rare to justify a new term.
The quality is 'narrow' and its bearer is the sinus: annotate leaf sinus (PO_0025384) with decreased width, not the leaf with a new term.
Two values run together: ovoid (PATO_0001891 ovate, EXACT synonym ovoid) and compressed = flattened (PATO_0002254); both apply to the same fruit.

'Petal/bract without claw' = not clawed: negation of FLOPO clawed.
In French floras 'sarmenteux' is the habit of woody plants with long, flexible shoots that lean on and scramble through other vegetation (often with 'lianescent'), so it maps to climbing.
The acumen is the acuminate tip; 'leaflet without acumen' = leaflet not acuminate.

A symbiotic association with fungi, not a morphological quality of the root. It belongs to an interaction or trait vocabulary, not PATO/FLOPO values.
A 'composite flower' is the head of the Asteraceae, a part (capitulum), not a quality.
A mode of nutrition (carnivory), not a quality of a plant structure. It is better recorded as a trait or a process than as a PATO-style value.
